recipes.name: Mom-Mom's Pepper Steak
ingredients_raw: 2 green bell peppers, cut into strips
2 red bell peppers, cut into strips
1.5 pounds round steak, cut into strips

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat, and cook and stir the green and red peppers until tender, about 10 minutes. Remove the peppers from the pan and set aside.

Place the steak strips into the skillet with the grated onion, and cook and stir for about 10 minutes, until the steak is evenly browned and no longer pink inside. Return the cooked peppers to the skillet, and stir in tomatoes, water, and sugar. Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer over low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the steak is tender and the sauce has thickened.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom-Mom's Pepper Steak
raw_recipe.description: Tender pieces of round steak are simmered with green and red peppers in a sweet tomato sauce.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was pretty good, but I did make 2 small changes to it. First, I added fresh minced garlic to the meat and onion mixture before putting the peppers back into the skillet. I also added a tablespoon of flour so that once I added the tomatoes and the water, it would make a thicker "gravy". This was pretty easy and my husband loved it! Thanks.

This was one of the most delicious comfort foods that I have ever eaten. I could see this being something that everyone looks forward to at Christmas made by some loving mother or grandmother. I did make some modifications per readers comments: added a clove of minced garlic and a tablespoon of flour, for thickening, just after browning the steak medium well. I also reduced the amount of sugar to just a pinch and cut the meat into bite sized chunks which I had coated with olive oil and peppercorn salt rub. I used one yellow and one red bell pepper which was plenty. Finally, I removed the lid on the pot for the last 15 minutes of cooking for reduction and thickening. One hour of cooking was plenty as the recipe calls for steak which tenderizes perfectly in a short time. Served over buttery mashed potatoes with a side of Italian bread and butter as recommended. It was heaven. I am so glad that I decided to take a chance of this when I went looking for a pepper steak recipe and will be making it again. It's good enough to become a tradition.

I loved this meal! I added diced tomatoes and made my own gravy for thickness. If you do not know how to make gravy here is what I did: after browning the meat (I did not cook the onions with the meat), I removed everything from the skillet. Then you put oil, onions, and flour in the pan..... keep stirring until the mixture browns. Then pour the natural juices from the steak into the pot while stirring vigorously! Add add extra water to the mixture if you desire thinner gravy or simply more gravy. Then you add your veggies and meat and finish cooking as the directions stated! It was very good

Good base recipe but lacks flavor. I added 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp of worcestershire, 1 tsp of dried thyme and an 8 oz can of tomato sauce. Additions took it up to 5 stars and would make again.

I put my steak in crock pot with peppers onion diced tomatoes ans tomatoe sauce cook on low for 8 hours add the salt pepper and garlic powder to eatch steak before you put in crock pot then as it's about done make mashed patato and cream corn yumm

Amazing recipe! Only change I made was to add a teaspoon of garlic to the steak and onion frying mixture. Then 1/3 cup of beef bullion with the tomatoes, water, and sugar (we like light sauce over rice). Surprisingly, kids loved it most of all!

This recipe is just like Mom's. Since I'm diabetic I didn't add the sugar, and served over mashed cauliflower. Hubby loved it and wants me to make it again. Oh, I added garlic too, just a personal preference.

I think this is a good base, no need to add water unless you add beef boullion and corn starch to thicken, (prior to adding to mixture), because you will end up with soup. I cant do tomatoes, I added 12oz of tomato sauce instead and 1-2 tsp of "Better than beef" boullion. I also used jar of crushed garlic, cooled with beef.
Served over jasmine rice on the sticky side. 
Delish! Unfortunately too hungry to get photo and between me & company, no leftovers. I will make again.

I've been looking for this recipe for quite a while. My mother used to make this and I loved it. I didn't have round steak so i used the elk steak I had and it was great. Didn't add water at all just used the juice in the diced tomatoes I added. Towards the end I added a tablespoon or so of flour to thicken the sauce and also added garlic because I love garlic.

I made this recipe but did a couple of changes - I sautéed the peppers first (they take longer to cook) removed them from the pan and added chopped onion and 3 cloves of crushed garlic then added the meat, I also added 2 beef bouillon cubes and some Worchester sauce and the crushed tomato and it came out thick and delicious

I admit to making a boo-boo but this still turned out tender and delicious. I thought I had a can of tomatoes but I didn't! I used a jar of Pace picante sauce and added a few dashes of worchestire sauce and was very pleased with the results. I cut sliced onion into thick rings and sautéed with pepper strips. Very tasty, and this was the first time I've made eye of round steaks (I sliced into strips) and they turned out tender, even without pounding. Will make again!
I loved this recipe it turned out great the only thing I changed was I sliced the onions
Used yellow and orange peppers, sliced onion, and a can of diced tomatoes. Turned out great!
